name: Broken Hill
note: Town (city): the region's regional centre and only city, a mining town with a Silver City heritage streetscape; base for Silverton, Mundi Mundi and the Far West parks. Destination-level.

name: Silverton
note: Town (ghost town, 26 km from Broken Hill): a Mad Max film location with a heritage walk and galleries; Wikivoyage Broken Hill lists it under Visit Silverton.

name: Menindee
note: Town: small Far West base on the Menindee Lakes, gateway to Kinchega National Park; Wikivoyage notes crime concerns and limited services.

name: Wilcannia
note: Town: Darling River town with a heritage centre of 1870-1890 buildings, a court house and an old sheet-iron theatre; Wikivoyage calls it very small.

name: Pooncarie
note: Town: small Darling River township, the gateway for Mungo National Park (about 80 km east); Wikivoyage lists little to see in town beyond the river.

name: Tibooburra
note: Town: remote outback town, base for Sturt National Park and the north-west corner of NSW; Wikivoyage lists its heritage stone buildings and museum.

name: White Cliffs
note: Town: small opal-mining village with underground living and a heritage trail; base for Paroo-Darling National Park.

name: Lightning Ridge
note: Town: the opal capital of NSW, with opal mines, the bore baths and the Car Door trail; the town is the base for its fields.

name: Bourke
note: Town: Darling River town, the only town for kilometres on the Kidman Way; base for Gundabooka National Park and the Back O Bourke country.

name: Cobar
note: Town: mining town in the centre of the NSW Outback with a heritage streetscape (Great Western Hotel verandah, court house) and an open-cut mine lookout.

name: Brewarrina
note: Town: Darling River town known for the Aboriginal fish traps and the Aboriginal Culture Museum; visitors come for the heritage.

name: Balranald
note: Town: Murrumbidgee-edge town with preserved homesteads and historic museums; gateway for Mungo National Park (about 120 km). Edge of the region; may also be judged under nsw-riverina-murray.

name: Wentworth
note: Town: where the Murray and Darling rivers meet (Wikivoyage Outback listing); edge of the region, may be judged under nsw-riverina-murray.

name: Mungo National Park
note: National park (UNESCO World Heritage, Willandra Lakes): the dry lakebed, Walls of China dunes and Mungo Man/Lady sites; drive loop, walks and guided tours. Destination-level.

name: Walls of China
note: Natural feature / viewing platform: the eroded lunette dunes of Mungo, the park's most iconic sight, seen from a wheelchair-accessible boardwalk; close-up views only on a guided tour.

name: Lake Mungo
note: Natural feature: the dry lake whose shores hold Mungo Lady and Mungo Man burial sites; seen from lookouts and the Foreshore walk. Part of Mungo National Park.

name: Mungo Lookout
note: Viewpoint over the dry Lake Mungo bed, with Walls of China in view; a sunset spot. Within Mungo National Park.

name: Red Top Lookout
note: Viewpoint and boardwalk on the Mungo drive loop with a different angle on the Walls of China dunes. Within Mungo National Park.
coordinates_source: approx: Walls of China viewing platform, Mungo (no OSM point found; replace with the visitor point)

name: Mungo Woolshed
note: Historic site: 1869 drop-log woolshed where 18 men sheared 75,000 sheep by hand on the Gol Gol station. Within Mungo National Park.

name: Zanci Homestead
note: Historic site: ruined homestead remains with a dugout larder and stables on the Zanci Pastoral Loop. Within Mungo National Park.

name: Mallee Stop Walk
note: Walking track: a 1 km (about 15-45 min) loop through grassy mallee on the Mungo drive. Within Mungo National Park; a trail section, judge against the park spot.
coordinates_source: approx: Mungo drive loop (no OSM point found; replace with the visitor point)

name: Mungo Foreshore Walk
note: Walking track: 2.5 km loop along the western shore of Lake Mungo, 45-75 min. Within Mungo National Park; a trail section.
coordinates_source: approx: Mungo lookout over Lake Mungo (no OSM point found; replace with the visitor point)

name: Mungo Walls of China Guided Tour
note: Operator tour (NPWS-run, about two hours, $50 adult per Wikivoyage): the only way to reach the Walls of China close up. An experience run by an operator; judge as an activity inside Mungo National Park.
coordinates_source: approx: Walls of China viewing platform (tour departs the visitor centre; no point found)

name: Kinchega National Park
note: National park: Menindee lake system and Darling River red gums, with historic woolshed and homestead sites; camping and Aboriginal discovery tours. Destination-level.

name: Kinchega Woolshed
note: Historic site: 1875 woolshed with presses and shearing machinery, free to see. Within Kinchega National Park.

name: Old Kinchega Homestead
note: Historic site: pastoral homestead ruins reached by a walkway. Within Kinchega National Park.

name: PS Providence Historic Site
note: Historic site: site of the 1872 boiler explosion of the paddle steamer PS Providence on the Darling River. Within Kinchega National Park; a minor plaque-scale site, judge closely.

name: Lake Cawndilla Dead Trees
note: Natural feature: dead river red gums in Lake Cawndilla, partly submerged at times, for views and photography. Within Kinchega National Park.

name: Menindee Lakes
note: Lake system: the Darling River storages that fill only after rain in Queensland, with birdlife; Wikivoyage names it as the reason to base at Menindee. Lake area, spans Kinchega and the town.

name: Barka Ngnugu
note: Unclear: listed under See in Menindee at 38 Darling St (Wikivoyage gives no description). Needs checking that it is an open public place to visit before judgement.

name: Mutawintji National Park
note: National park (Bynguano Ranges, red-coloured hills north-east of Broken Hill): one of the best Aboriginal rock art collections in NSW, guided tours of the historic site, camping. Destination-level.

name: Mutawintji Historic Site
note: Historic site: hand-stencil rock art and Dreamtime stories, reached by a booked guided tour (Mutawintji Board of Management). Within Mutawintji National Park.

name: Mutawintji Gorge Walk
note: Walking track: a more challenging gorge walk in Mutawintji National Park, with the Rockholes Loop as its companion track.

name: Thaaklatjika Mingkana Walk
note: Walking track: an easy walk in Mutawintji National Park, named in NPWS's walking list. Trail section.

name: Sturt National Park

name: Mount Wood Summit Walk
note: Walking track and summit: NPWS names Mount Wood hills as the walk to do if you only have time for one, with stunning views. Within Sturt National Park.

name: Gorge Loop Road
note: Scenic drive: a 104 km round-trip self-guided road through the park, 2-3 hours; a route rather than a place. Within Sturt National Park.

name: Fort Grey Loop Walk

name: Cameron Corner Survey Marker

name: Tibooburra Granite Tors
note: Natural feature: 450-million-year-old granite tors around Tibooburra, with the Sunset Hill lookout nearby. Visible from the park roads.

name: Outdoor Pastoral Museum
note: Museum: outdoor display of a 19th-century settler farm, on a diversion from the Gorge Loop Road. Within Sturt National Park.

name: Sunset Hill Lookout
note: Viewpoint: lookout above Tibooburra over the granite country, a short drive from town.

note: Museum: local Aboriginal artefacts, language and fossils, with the story of the oldest continuous culture.

name: Mundi Mundi Lookout
